newsitem.title: CHINA: China reforms seen creating a buyer's market.
newsitem.headline: China reforms seen creating a buyer's market.

text.p: Economic reforms in the past five years have led to the supply of consumer goods far exceeding demand, changing China from a seller's to a buyer's market, a leading economist was quoted as saying on Thursday.

"In the past five years, China's market has undergone tremendous changes," Ma Hong was quoted by the Business News as saying. "The whole economy shows signs of supply far exceeding demand, making China an overall buyers' market."

The developments had seen China's economy become more closely related to the world economy with a reliance ratio on the international market now around 40 percent compared with about 10 percent five years ago, Ma said.
Consumer prices had become more market-driven with prices of about 85 percent of industrial commodities and 95 percent of daily commodities now decided by the market, Ma said.
The major problem currently facing China's economy was the poor performance of the state-run enterprises, he said.
Demand for their products was weak and their management was unsuited to the market economy, he said.
Official figures show that more than 40 percent of China's state companies are losing money.
